es: Comprender relatos de malentendidos culturales e identificar qué esperaba cada persona, cómo lo interpretó y cuál fue la causa.

teaching.en: Living abroad taught me that a simple gesture can mean different things.
teaching.es: Vivir en el extranjero me enseñó que un simple gesto puede significar cosas distintas.
teaching.explanationEs: Abroad = en otro país; un gesture puede cambiar de significado según la cultura.
segments: Living abroad taught me that a
simple gesture can mean different things.
teaching.audioText: Living abroad taught me that a simple gesture can mean different things.

teaching.en: She assumed that everybody would shake hands, but her new colleagues only smiled.
teaching.es: Ella supuso que todos se darían la mano, pero sus nuevos compañeros solo sonrieron.
teaching.explanationEs: Assumed + that marca una expectativa que luego no se cumple.
segments: She assumed that everybody would shake hands,
but her new colleagues only smiled.
teaching.audioText: She assumed that everybody would shake hands, but her new colleagues only smiled.

teaching.en: My host was offended when I refused a second plate of food.
teaching.es: Mi anfitriona se ofendió cuando rechacé un segundo plato de comida.
teaching.explanationEs: Offended describe cómo se sintió la persona; la causa suele ir con by o when.
segments: My host was offended when I
refused a second plate of food.
teaching.audioText: My host was offended when I refused a second plate of food.

teaching.en: In his country a blunt answer shows honesty, but here it sounded rude.
teaching.es: En su país una respuesta directa muestra honestidad, pero aquí sonó descortés.
teaching.explanationEs: Blunt = sin rodeos; lo que es positivo en una cultura puede sonar mal en otra.
segments: In his country a blunt answer shows
honesty, but here it sounded rude.
teaching.audioText: In his country a blunt answer shows honesty, but here it sounded rude.

teaching.en: I felt embarrassed because I had arrived on the wrong day.
teaching.es: Me sentí avergonzado porque había llegado el día equivocado.
teaching.explanationEs: Embarrassed describe lo que siente la persona; no se dice embarrassing para uno mismo.
segments: I felt embarrassed because I had
teaching.audioText: I felt embarrassed because I had arrived on the wrong day.

teaching.en: The misunderstanding came from different expectations, not from bad manners.
teaching.es: El malentendido vino de expectativas distintas, no de mala educación.
teaching.explanationEs: Casi siempre la causa es una diferencia de expectations y no de manners.
teaching.audioText: The misunderstanding came from different expectations, not from bad manners.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué se molestó la anfitriona de Ana?

choices.text: She wanted Ana to leave early.
She had no more food.
She thought Ana disliked the meal.

feedback.es: Ana rechazó el segundo plato por cortesía, pero la anfitriona lo interpretó como que no le gustaba la comida.

hint.es: Fíjate en cómo interpretó la anfitriona el rechazo de Ana.

origin.text: Interviewer: Why did your host look upset? Ana: I refused a second plate of food. I thought I was being polite, but she took it as a sign that I disliked the meal.

prompt.es: Completa: «Supuse que la cena empezaba a las ocho.»

feedback.es: Assumed que + oración expresa lo que das por hecho sin comprobarlo.

hint.es: Es el verbo de la clase para dar algo por hecho.

origin.text: I ___ that dinner started at eight.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La causa fueron expectativas distintas, no mala educación.»

answer.text: The cause was different expectations not bad manners

feedback.es: La causa de un malentendido cultural suele ser una diferencia de expectativas, no de modales.

hint.es: Empieza por la causa y cierra con la contraposición not bad manners.

choices.text: That they were unfriendly.
That they were very busy.
That they wanted him to leave.

feedback.es: Leo pensó que sus compañeros eran antipáticos; después supo que el gesto era un saludo cálido.

origin.text: Leo: On my first day, my new colleagues gave me a small nod. I thought they were unfriendly, so I stayed quiet. Later I learned that a nod is a warm greeting there.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál fue la causa del malentendido de Sara.

choices.text: A rude comment from her boss.
Different ideas about being on time.
A mistake in the invitation.

feedback.es: Sara entendió que la causa era una idea distinta del tiempo, no una falta de respeto.

origin.audio: Sara explains that in her country people arrive on time for a meeting, but in her new office colleagues usually arrive ten minutes late. At first she felt offended, but then she understood the reason: a different view of time.

prompt.es: Completa con: gesto · en el extranjero · avergonzada

feedback.es: Un gesto cambia de significado, abroad es vivir en otro país y embarrassed describe la vergüenza que siente la persona.

sentences: A simple ___ can mean different things in different places.
After moving ___, she learned many new customs.
She felt ___ when she realised she had spoken too loudly.

prompt.es: ¿Qué causó el malentendido entre Mia y sus compañeros de casa?

choices.text: They did not like her cooking.
They were too busy to eat.
They showed thanks in a different way.

feedback.es: Sus compañeros agradecían comiendo mucho y pidiendo repetir, no diciendo thank you.

origin.text: Mia: My flatmates never said thank you when I cooked. I thought they did not care. Then I learned that, in their families, people show thanks by eating a lot and asking for more.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se adaptó Carlos.

choices.text: He changed the way he gave his opinions.
He stopped talking to his boss.
He moved to another country.

feedback.es: Carlos pasó de decir las cosas sin rodeos a proponer ideas con una fórmula más suave.

origin.audio: Carlos says that when he told his colleagues exactly what he thought, they felt offended. So he changed his style and began to say things like: I wonder whether another idea might work.

prompt.es: ¿Qué aprende Ana sobre llamar a la profesora por su nombre?

choices.text: That it is always rude.
That it is normal there and not rude.
That teachers dislike it.

feedback.es: La profesora le explica que es normal allí: Ana suponía una falta de respeto que no existía.

origin.text: Ana: In my new school, students call the teacher by her first name. I was shocked and thought it was rude. The teacher explained that it is normal here.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se sintió avergonzada porque dio por hecho algo equivocado.»

answer.text: She felt embarrassed because she assumed the wrong thing

feedback.es: La frase une la emoción (embarrassed) con su causa (assumed the wrong thing) mediante because.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase explica la causa de un malentendido cultural?

choices.text: One person was tired and forgot the invitation.
The food arrived cold and nobody ate it.
Each person expected something different from the situation.

feedback.es: La causa de un malentendido cultural es que cada persona esperaba algo distinto, no un olvido ni un accidente.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los invitados se ofendieron por su comentario.»

feedback.es: Con offended la causa se introduce con by o at, no con for.

origin.text: The guests were offended ___ his comment.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo terminó el malentendido de Leo.

choices.text: Someone explained the custom, and Leo stopped feeling upset.
Leo left his job because nobody explained anything.
Leo's boss apologised to the whole office.

feedback.es: La explicación del compañero resolvió el malentendido y Leo dejó de sentirse molesto.

origin.audio: Leo says the misunderstanding ended when a colleague explained the custom. After that, Leo was not upset any more; he laughed and said thank you.
